name: Lightweight volcanic stone in Rome’s concrete vaults
description: Builders in Rome used light volcanic rock, including scoria and yellow tuff, as coarse aggregate in concrete vaults. They set the pieces of stone, or caementa, into mortar to form a lighter vault.

date.label: Approximately 46–44 BCE
date.basis: Lancaster et al. date the room context to 46–44 BCE.

events.statement: Dark volcanic scoria was used as coarse aggregate in a room vault facing the portico of the Forum of Caesar.

evidence.supports: The authors describe and photograph dark scoria caementa in the room vault and assign its room context to 46–44 BCE.

date.label: By 112 CE
date.basis: Lancaster et al. date the sampled Basilica Ulpia vault fragment by the building’s date of 112 CE.

events.statement: Builders of the Basilica Ulpia used alternating layers of yellow tuff and dark scoria as coarse aggregate in a north aisle vault.

evidence.supports: The study describes the mix of coarse aggregate and dates the basilica to 112 CE.
The archaeological description identifies alternating tuff and dark scoria courses in a collapsed vault fragment assigned to a north aisle.

date.label: Approximately 298–305 CE
date.basis: Lancaster et al. date the Baths of Diocletian context to 298–305 CE.

events.statement: The buttressing arches of the frigidarium at the Baths of Diocletian used pumiceous scoria as coarse aggregate. Geochemical analysis linked the sampled stone to the Campi Flegrei volcanic district.

evidence.supports: The authors identify the material, building context and date, and associate the trace-element ratios of the analysed sample with Campi Flegrei.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated sampled case in this record, assigned to a room at the Forum of Caesar.

caveats: The sampled cases concern the large pieces of volcanic rock in the vault or arch concrete. Fine ash or pumice mixed into mortar was a separate ingredient.

unresolved.note: The date assigned to the Forum of Caesar sample depends on its room phase. Check Amici’s room-level phasing and any newer stratigraphic report before assigning priority. The reason for the later change in aggregate source remains open.

evidence.supports: The study dates the earliest sampled scoria by its room context and asks why the later material source changed.
